claims.text: The starting material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The stated high-temperature yield-strength range applies at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxidation resistance and undergoes rapid oxidation at high temperature.
Pack cementation can deposit aluminum onto the surface of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited aluminum will oxidize during high-temperature exposure to form an Al2O3 surface scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be thin and uniform.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be stable and adherent on HfNbTaTiZr.
An Al2O3 surface layer will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier and reduce oxidation of the underlying alloy.
Aluminised HfNbTaTiZr will have markedly lower oxygen uptake than untreated HfNbTaTiZr after high-temperature exposure.
Aluminised HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit less surface oxidation than untreated HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminisation treatment will leave the bulk microstructure unaffected.
The treatment will preserve the room-temperature tensile ductility of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The treatment will preserve the high-temperature yield strength of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed performance boundary is a 100-hour exposure at 1000 °C in air or a controlled oxygen atmosphere.
The surface treatment must not induce additional phases or detrimental microstructural changes in the alloy bulk.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe the 100-hour oxidation exposure as occurring under mechanical loading at specified strain rates, whereas the experiment describes oxidation first and mechanical testing afterward, implying a sequential unloaded exposure.
